 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 20.06.2022.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 20.06.2022 at about 10.00am, while the Petitioner was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA53Y 9911 from Pattegarapalya main Road to Thrimurthi Junction on the left side of the road, when he reached near Petrol bunk, a Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA04C9547 came with high speed, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed against the petitioner. Due to this accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Triveni Hospital, Vijayanagar, Bangalore, wherein took first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to ProMed Hospital, Banashankari, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient,
surgery was done and discharged with advice. So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards surgery and medical expenses, nourishment and transportation expenses. 
4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy,
working as a Programme Operator at Arotech System Company and earning Rs.26,240/ per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he suffered permanent disablement as such till Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/
2 now unable to report to duty. He is put to great financial hardship and untold misery. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA04C9547 and the Vijayanagara Traffic police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.0066/2022 punishable u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC. The 1st Respondent being the Insurer and the 2 nd respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition. 
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement. In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.2 did not appear. Hence, placed exparte. 
6. The objections of the Respondent No.1: 
It has denied all the petitioner averments. It has denied that the vehicle bearing No.KA04C9547 was insured with this respondent and the insurance was not in force at the time of alleged accident. The driver of the Tempo Traveler did not possess valid DL as on the date of accident and the vehicular documents such as FC and Permit are also not update as on the date of alleged accident. There is non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act. Further stated that the rider/Petitioner was riding the two wheeler without valid driving license and vehicle documents and in a rash and negligent manner and had self fall and given false complaint against the driver of the vehicle belonging to the 2 nd respondent. The delay in lodging the police complaint itself indicates the aspect. This Respondent insurer has further denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age, occupation, income and other details of the Petitioner and has sought for dismissal of the petition. 
7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 20.06.2022 at about 10.00am, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA04C 9547 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries? 
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum? From whom payable? 
3. What order or award? 
8. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to P.14. Dr. Nagaraj B.N. - Orthopedics, Sai Ortho and Dental Center got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.15 &
16. On the other side, the Respondent No.1 has got examined Mr.Ramesh P.  Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to 3.
Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/
3 9. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties. 
The learned counsel for the Petitioner has relied upon the following decision:
Misc. First Appeal No.388/2013 (MVSJ) : National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Mallikarjuna. 
The learned counsel for the Respondent No.1 has filed written arguments. 
10. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 11. Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveler Reg.No.KA04C9547 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 4 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 4. PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination. The Respondent No.1 has denied the manner of accident and also denied the negligence and rash driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the self fall of the petitioner. In the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile showing the absence of negligence on the part of the driver of Tempo is elicited. 
12. The FIR was registered on 20.06.2022 on the complaint of petitioner on the same day of accident at Ex . P.1 . Ex . P.2 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending Tempo Traveler after thorough investigation. Ex.P.4 MVA report shows that petitioner's vehicle damaged to its indicator, silencer pipe, front safety guard, left side become bend, headlight mask scratched, rear seat belt both covers, rear indicator, rear side foot rest, right side shield, rear tail bend and damaged.
Exs.P.3 & 7 are the Wound Certificate and discharge summary of ProMed Hospital show that the petitioner diagnosed with right humerus shaft lower 1/3rd fracture which is grievous in nature. The respondent No.1 got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.3 Authorization letter, insurance policy and charge sheet. During the cross examination of RW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited. Therefore, on the basis of oral evidence of PW.1 and RW.1 and the police documents on record, the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA04C9547. Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative. 
13. Issue No.2: In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the Wound Certificate as per Ex.3. As per Ex.P.3, the Petitioner has sustained Right Humerus shaft lower 1/3rd fracture which is grievous in nature. 
14. The Petitioner also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2. He has deposed the details of surgery of the right lower 1/3rd humerus and has stated about the disability of the right Arm at 37% and to Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/
4 the whole body at 12%. PW.2 has produced 2 documents as per Exs.P.15 & 16 clinical and recent X ray. 
15. In his cross examination, PW.2 stated that, he has not treated the petitioner. Before assessing disability, he has gone through the wound certificate and discharge summary. He has subjected the petitioner to Xray and clinical examination and as per Xray fractures are united. He has admitted that the condition of the petitioner has considerably improved from the date of discharge to date of assessment of disability. From the evidence of PW.2 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact on his work as Programme Operator. Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to consider the whole body disability at 12%. 
Monthly income:
16. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Programme Operator at Arotech System Company and earning Rs.26,240/ per month. In this regard he has produced pay slips for the months of March, April and May 2022 as per Ex.P.9. To show the corresponding entries, he has produced only the first page of the Pass Book without producing the Bank statement or any other document and also not examined his employer in support of it. The petitioner has studied upto 2nd PUC. The accident occurred in the year 2022. Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/ per month. 
17. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 28 years as could be made out from the affidavit as well as Exs.P.10 & 11/DL and Aadhar Card. He was hale and healthy before the accident. 
Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING: After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Triveni Hospital and ProMed hospital Bangalore as an inpatient from 20.06.2022 to 22.06.2022 and discharged with advice to take follow up treatment. In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.7 discharge summary of ProMed Hospital, Bangalore. Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous,
the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/ under this head. 
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc., In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.5 for a sum of Rs.2,17,647/. As per the details of Bills, there is an advance bills at Sl.Nos.2 to 4 total amount of Rs.1,00,000/ which are paid under Sl.No.13. Therefore, the above said bills have to be deducted in total expenses. After deduction of the above said amount of Rs.1,00,000/, then the balance amount comes to Rs.1,17,647/. Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head. 
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD: As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. The petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days at ProMed Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.7 Discharge summary. Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/
5 duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him. Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/ under this head. 
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME: On perusal of Exs.P.10 & 11/DL and Aadhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is 26.04.1994 and the accident occurred on 20.06.2022. As per these documents petitioner's age was 28 years as on the date of accident. As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17. As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,79,440/. (Rs.15,500/ x 12 x 12% x 17 = Rs.3,79,440/ ). 
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS: 
The Petitioner was aged about 28 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous injury and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 12% functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts. Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.30,000/ is awarded under this head. 
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 3 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise. However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head. 
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implant and the estimated cost of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/. In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 have not produced any bills. Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head. Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head. 
18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.60,000/
2. Medical expenses Rs.1,17,647/
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.15,500/
Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/
6 4. Loss of future income Rs.3,79,440/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.6,42,587/ If it is rounded off it comes around //Rs.6,42,600/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner. 
LIABILITY 21. The respondent No.1 has contended that the accident was caused due to self fall when the petitioner was drunk. However, They did not prove their defence. The counsel for the petitioner has reliedupon the decision Misc. First Appeal No.388/2013 (MVSJ) : National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. 
Mallikarjuna . 
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, 'the insurer cannot avoid his liability to satisfy the award under Sec.149 of MV Act on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was drunk'. 
Therefore, the contention of the respondent No.1 does not hold any water. Hence, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending Tempo Traveler are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Though the petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.12,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,42,600/ with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. Therefore, the petition needs to allowed. Accordingly, issue No.2 held in the Affirmative. 
22. Issue No.4: For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER The petition is allowed with cost. 
 The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.6,42,600/ (Rupees Six Lakhs Forty Two Thousand and Six Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner. 
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award. 
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.

7 Draw decree accordingly.

He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Triveni Hospital and ProMed hospital Bangalore as an inpatient from 20.06.2022 to 22.06.2022 and discharged with advice to take follow up treatment.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.7 discharge summary of ProMed Hospital, Bangalore.

Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous,
the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.5 for a sum of Rs.2,17,647/.
As per the details of Bills, there is an advance bills at Sl.Nos.2 to 4 total amount of Rs.1,00,000/ which are paid under Sl.No.13.
Therefore, the above said bills have to be deducted in total expenses.
After deduction of the above said amount of Rs.1,00,000/, then the balance amount comes to Rs.1,17,647/.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days at ProMed Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.7 Discharge summary.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/
5 duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
On perusal of Exs.P.10 & 11/DL and Aadhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is 26.04.1994 and the accident occurred on 20.06.2022.
As per these documents petitioner's age was 28 years as on the date of accident.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.
As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,79,440/.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 28 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injury and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 12% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.30,000/ is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 3 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implant and the estimated cost of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 have not produced any bills.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:

The respondent No.1 has contended that the accident was caused due to self fall when the petitioner was drunk.
However, They did not prove their defence.
The counsel for the petitioner has reliedupon the decision
Misc. First Appeal No.388/2013 (MVSJ) : National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs.

. 
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, 'the insurer cannot avoid his liability to satisfy the award under Sec.149 of MV Act on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was drunk'.
Therefore, the contention of the respondent No.1 does not hold any water.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending Tempo Traveler are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

The petition is allowed with cost.

The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
